enforced_dimensions.max_entries: security/limits.py, security/sanitizer.py, security/trust.py -- enforced incrementally during parsing (bounded_object_pairs_hook), not only after full materialization

not_applicable_dimensions.max_header_bytes: no fixed-size binary header in this format

evidence.key_proof: test_a_single_oversized_object_is_rejected_before_full_materialization and test_many_separate_objects_are_rejected_on_the_cumulative_running_total both prove enforcement happens incrementally during json.loads' own object_pairs_hook, not after the full document is already materialized in memory -- a 200,000-key object with max_entries=5 is refused without ever building the full dict.

note: This is one of product-goal.yaml's own 10 completion invariants (installed-wheel, independent-oracle, corpus, security, resource, typing, documentation, compatibility, performance, reproducible-build) -- this file consolidates already-existing, already-passing resource-limit evidence into a dedicated gate record; not a certification claim for the format as a whole.
